Prism Assistant¶

The Prism Assistant is an MCP server that lets an AI assistant, such as Claude Code or Claude Desktop, help you with your Prism/Lente project. It runs on your computer, in your scripts repo, and gives the AI assistant read-only tools for this documentation, your scripts, the drivers and the Prism APIs.

It can help you,

  • migrate to a new Prism/Lente version, for example 0.8 to 0.9

  • write test scripts and Python test code, and lint them

  • use BOND

  • add test equipment to a jig, one per jig or shared by the jigs, see Drivers

  • lay out your test plan and test stages

  • plan Traceability: serial numbers, lots, firmware versions and test versions

  • plan and install the Prism and Lente computers of your deployment

Install¶

The assistant is in the assistant folder of the scripts repo, and uses the Python virtual environment from Installing Python,

cd ~/git/scripts
source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -r assistant/requirements.txt

Check the server starts, it waits for a client on stdin, stop it with Ctrl-C,

python assistant/prism_assistant.py

Connect an AI Assistant¶

Claude Code reads .mcp.json at the top of the scripts repo, which starts the assistant from .venv. Start Claude Code in the repo, approve the prism-assistant server when asked, and check it with /mcp.

Claude Desktop and other MCP clients need the full paths, for example in Claude Desktop’s claude_desktop_config.json,

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "prism-assistant": {
      "command": "/home/me/git/scripts/.venv/bin/python",
      "args": ["/home/me/git/scripts/assistant/prism_assistant.py"]
    }
  }
}

The assistant works on the scripts repo it is in. To use it with another repo, set the environment variable PRISM_REPO to that repo’s folder.

Using It¶

Ask your question in the AI assistant, for example “how do I store the firmware version of my DUT?”, or “lint my BLT script”. The assistant looks up the answer in the documentation and your repo.

The assistant also has prompts for longer tasks. In Claude Code they are slash commands, for example /mcp__prism-assistant__migrate_version,

  • migrate_version - plan a version migration of your deployment

  • write_test_script - write a script and its test code for one test stage

  • review_test_script - review a script and its test code, see Script Design

  • use_bond - design the Pogo board from the template, set up BOND and its Pogo board header definition

  • analyze_coverage - analyse which faults the test detects on each part of a PCBA, see PCBA Test Coverage

  • add_equipment - add test equipment to a jig, one per jig or shared, with its driver

  • plan_test_stages - lay out the test stages of a product

  • plan_traceability - plan what your results record

  • plan_deployment - plan and install Lente and the Prism computers

  • setup_prism_computer - set up and check one Prism computer

The tools the AI assistant can use,

  • list_docs, read_doc, search_docs - this documentation, and the driver and example READMEs

  • read_file - read files in your scripts repo

  • list_scripts, lint_script - your scripts, and the Script Lint

  • check_settings - check a settings.json for the current version, without showing any passwords or keys

  • list_drivers, python_api - the drivers with their documentation, and the Prism APIs used by test code

  • repo_status - your scripts version, and how far your fork is behind Sistemi’s scripts

What the Assistant Is Told¶

When the AI assistant connects, the server gives it instructions. In short, the AI assistant,

  • is helping you with your Prism/Lente project, not developing Prism or Lente

  • answers from this documentation and your repo, cites the page, and says so when they don’t have the answer, instead of guessing, suggesting you contact info@sistemi.ca

  • lints any script or test code it writes or changes

  • writes scripts as a list of tests with their limits, that a technician can change without a programmer, and keeps the test code simple, see Script Design

  • analyses test coverage per part (Short, Open, Value) and per IC pin (Short, Open), and only counts a fault as covered when it moves a measurement outside the limits

  • records the serial number of each piece of test equipment in the results, see Test Equipment, and follows the driver rules for equipment per jig or shared

  • starts a Pogo board from the template, see Designing the Pogo Board, and leaves your BOND’s population options to you and the BOND schematic

  • follows the rules in this documentation, for example the test item rules, the serial number in key0, and Prism and Lente running the same major.minor version

  • never asks you for passwords, the site_key, license files or user databases, and never suggests committing real passwords to your repo

  • keeps your code and data in the conversation, and proposes small changes it explains

  • numbers its questions, so you can answer them easily

The full text is INSTRUCTIONS in assistant/prism_assistant.py.

Privacy¶

  • The assistant only reads files, it does not change your repo. The AI assistant may still change files with its own tools, review those changes as you would any other.

  • What the tools return is sent to your AI assistant’s provider, like anything else you share with it. Your scripts and test code are your own, check your company’s policy before using an AI assistant with them.

  • settings.json files, keys, certificates, the license file, user databases, results, logs and public/tools are never read. check_settings reports problems without the values.

The AI assistant can be wrong. Check its answers against this documentation, and test changes with prism_dev.py before production. For questions the documentation does not answer, contact info@sistemi.ca.
